items.headline: COE premiums fall across most categories in the second June bidding exercise
items.summary: At the June 17 close, premiums dipped in four of five categories: Category B fell S$3,487 to S$123,502 and Category A eased S$2,162 to S$123,847, with school-holiday demand softer.

items.headline: Singapore to review its waste blueprint as recycling slips and Semakau fills up
items.summary: With recycling rates drifting from national targets, the authorities will review the Zero Waste Masterplan to stretch the lifespan of the Semakau landfill, which is projected to run out of space around 2035.

items.headline: Singapore Cruise Centre to move ferry and cruise operations to a new HarbourFront terminal
items.summary: All ferry and cruise services will shift to a new HarbourFront terminal in two phases from July 7, with no changes to existing routes, destinations or schedules.

items.headline: Singapore shares edge up as the Straits Times Index gains about 0.7%
items.summary: The benchmark Straits Times Index rose around 0.7% to about 5,213 on June 18, tracking firmer regional sentiment even as several index heavyweights slipped.

items.headline: Jio Platforms files for a mega IPO after its board clears the DRHP at the Reliance AGM
items.summary: At Reliance Industries' 49th AGM on June 19, Mukesh Ambani said Jio Platforms' board had approved its draft red herring prospectus, filed with SEBI the same day, offering 27 crore fresh shares; RIL also declared a Rs 6 dividend.

items.headline: Sensex slides 608 points and the Nifty ends at 24,013 as IT stocks lead a selloff
items.summary: Indian benchmarks snapped a five-day winning run on June 19, with the Sensex down 0.78% to 76,803 and the Nifty 50 off 0.64% to 24,013, dragged by Infosys, TCS and Tech Mahindra after Accenture's weak outlook.

items.headline: South Delhi doctor arrested over the killing of his domestic helper
items.summary: Police said dermatologist Manish Gupta was arrested after his domestic helper, Meena, was found dead at a Mount Kailash flat on June 18; he allegedly attacked her, telling investigators he believed she brought 'bad energy' to his home.

items.headline: IMD says the monsoon will advance across more of east and central India by June 23
items.summary: The India Meteorological Department forecast the southwest monsoon to cover more of Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha and Chhattisgarh by around June 23, even as Delhi sweltered with highs near 42 degrees Celsius on June 19.

items.headline: Meloni rejects Trump's claim she begged for a photo as Italy cancels a US visit
items.summary: Italian PM Giorgia Meloni said she was 'stunned' by Trump's claim that she begged him for a photo at the G7, calling it made up; Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani cancelled a June 21-22 trip to Washington.

items.headline: Trump unveils a Qatar-gifted Boeing 747 as the new Air Force One
items.summary: Trump showed off a refitted, Qatari-donated Boeing 747-8 at Joint Base Andrews on June 19, a roughly $400 million jet the US accepted as a gift; the White House says it will pass to his presidential library foundation after he leaves office.

items.headline: Andy Burnham wins a by-election, returning to Parliament to set up a Starmer challenge
items.summary: Greater Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham won the Makerfield by-election with 24,927 votes, beating Reform UK's Robert Kenyon by more than 9,000, giving him a Commons seat from which to mount a Labour leadership bid against Keir Starmer.

items.headline: Cuba's Communist Party approves an emergency plan to open the economy
items.summary: Cuba's Communist Party approved unprecedented free-market measures, widening private enterprise and foreign investment and allowing private real estate development, as a Trump-imposed oil blockade pushes the island toward economic collapse.

items.headline: EU leaders agree their first joint Ukraine conclusions since early 2025
items.summary: At a June 18-19 summit in Brussels, the 27 EU leaders endorsed joint conclusions on Ukraine for the first time since March 2025, urging Russia to accept an immediate ceasefire, and backed tougher action on China.

items.headline: Waymo recalls nearly 4,000 robotaxis after cars drove into freeway construction zones
items.summary: Waymo recalled about 3,900 robotaxis running its 5th-generation software after vehicles failed to recognise ramp closures in roughly a dozen incidents in Phoenix and the San Francisco Bay Area, and temporarily barred them from freeways while it issues a fix.

items.headline: Meta strikes 1.6-gigawatt AI computing deals with data-centre firm Crusoe
items.summary: Meta agreed to buy about 1.6 gigawatts of computing capacity from Crusoe across data centres in Childress, Texas, and Warrenton, Missouri, deepening the infrastructure behind its AI push.

items.headline: AI inference startup Baseten is reportedly raising $1.5 billion at a $13 billion valuation
items.summary: Baseten is close to a $1.5 billion round that would value it at about $13 billion, just five months after a $300 million Series E at a $5 billion valuation, with Spark, Sands, Altimeter and Wellington co-leading.

items.headline: Apple's Tim Cook says price increases are unavoidable amid an AI-driven memory shortage
items.summary: Cook told the Wall Street Journal that surging AI demand for DRAM and NAND chips has made device price increases unavoidable, comparing the squeeze to a 'hundred-year flood,' though he did not say which products would rise or when.

items.headline: Bank of England holds its rate at 3.75% in a 7-2 vote as inflation eases
items.summary: The Monetary Policy Committee kept Bank Rate at 3.75%, with two members voting for a hike to 4%, after May inflation eased to 2.8%, below forecasts, while energy-price risks from the Iran conflict lingered.

items.headline: Wall Street rebounds as the Nasdaq jumps about 1.9% after the Fed-driven selloff
items.summary: US stocks recovered on June 18, with the Nasdaq up about 1.9%, the S&P 500 up 1.1% and the Russell 2000 up 2.1%, as Treasury yields eased and Trump's interim Iran deal steadied sentiment.

items.headline: Kroger's quarterly sales top estimates at $46.1 billion as e-commerce jumps 19%
items.summary: Kroger reported first-quarter sales of $46.1 billion, ahead of forecasts, with adjusted EPS of $1.58 and adjusted e-commerce sales up 19%, and maintained its full-year guidance even as margins narrowed.

items.headline: Gold slips below $4,200 an ounce as a hawkish Fed offsets the Iran peace boost
items.summary: Gold fell below $4,200 on June 19, erasing the week's gains, after the Fed signalled possible rate hikes; Brent crude eased to about $79 a barrel as Gulf supply risks receded.

items.headline: Eala beats Svitolina to reach the Berlin Open semifinals
items.summary: Wild card Alexandra Eala followed her upset of Elena Rybakina by beating Elina Svitolina 6-3, 6-4 to reach the Berlin grass-court semifinals.

items.headline: Pegula edges Keys in two tiebreaks to make the Berlin semifinals
items.summary: Jessica Pegula beat Madison Keys 7-6(5), 7-6(8) to reach the Berlin semifinals, where she meets Alexandra Eala.

items.headline: Zverev saves two set points to reach the Halle semifinals
items.summary: Top seed Alexander Zverev beat qualifier Raphael Collignon 7-6(10), 7-6(3), saving set points in the opening tie-break, to reach the Halle semifinals.

items.headline: Fritz saves a match point against Shelton to set up a Zverev semifinal
items.summary: Taylor Fritz hit 24 aces and saved a match point to beat Ben Shelton in three tie-break sets at Halle, setting up a semifinal against Alexander Zverev.

items.headline: New Zealand edge Ireland by four runs at the Women's T20 World Cup
items.summary: New Zealand defended a modest total to beat Ireland by four runs at Southampton for their first win of the tournament; Orla Prendergast (59) and captain Gaby Lewis (58) fell just short in the chase.

fun_fact.headline: The birthday paradox: 23 people, even odds of a shared birthday
fun_fact.body: In a group of just 23 people, there is a better-than-even chance - about 50.7% - that two of them share the same birthday. With 70 people the odds climb above 99.9%. The result is so counterintuitive that mathematicians call it the 'birthday paradox.'

puzzle.title: Triangles within the Triangle
puzzle.body: A large equilateral triangle has each side divided into 4 equal parts, with lines drawn parallel to all three sides, splitting it into 16 small congruent triangles (an upward-pointing grid 4 rows tall). How many triangles of all sizes can you count in the whole figure?
puzzle.approach: Count by size and orientation - tally upward-pointing triangles from smallest to largest, then the downward-pointing ones.
puzzle.answer: 27. Upward-pointing: size 1 = 10, size 2 = 6, size 3 = 3, size 4 = 1 (20). Downward-pointing: size 1 = 6, size 2 = 1 (7). 20 + 7 = 27.
